text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower, but well off earlier lows seen as it reacted to a slide in New York. October lost 80 cents to close at $327.50 per tonne, while December gave up $1.30 to close at $322.50 per tonne. There were no fresh fundamental news to give the market direction.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed lower across the board with October and March losing 8 points to close at 11.58 and 11.78 cents/lb respectively. The market remained extremely dull with no significant changes forecast for 1997/98. FUNDAMENTALS

KENYA ** - Sugar production in Kenya in 1998 is forecast to rise to 485,000 tonnes, tel quel, up from an estimated 462,000 tonnes this year and 420,000 tonnes produced in 1996. Consumption remained stagnant at 560,000 tonnes as in the last two years. The Kenyan sugar industry is suffering from low cost imports which are partly marked under transit but end up on the local market. But the industry remains optimistic that production will continue to grow with the total in 1999 expected to reach 510,000 tonnes.

Czech Republic ** - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 1,419 tonnes, raw value, down from 2,495 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first nine months of 1996/97 (September/May) up to 10,810 tonnes compared to 13,096 tonnes in 1995/96. The major country of origin in January/May 1997 was Germany with 2,451 tonnes whites.

Sugar exports in May 1997 reached 6,549 tonnes, up from last year's 1,585 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in September/May 1996/97 up to 60,571 tonnes compared to 18,787 shipped in the same year ago period. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 27,684 compared to 35,029 in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in January/May 1997 were Poland with 23,696 tonnes whites and Slovakia with 2,968 tonnes.

Denmark ** - The weather in the week ended July 27 was reported to be good with local showers and only few hours of sunshine. Temperatures were above the long-term mean. The precipitation level since April ranges between 165-232 mm compared and average of 185-195 mm. Beet growth is considered to be very good. Aphid attacks are reported from some growing regions but overall impact of pests and diseases is considered to be negligible. The overall crop prospect is normal.

The European Union awarded 35,600 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 39.057 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on July 30. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to July 30 reached 2,530,025 tonnes, which compares to 2,535,898 tonnes last year.
